newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cabinet approves Chidambaram's budget.
newsitem.headline: Indian cabinet approves Chidambaram's budget.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's cabinet on Thursday adopted the 1997/98 (April-March) budget which had been presented to parliament by former finance minister P. Chidambaram.

An official spokesman told reporters that the government looked forward to parliament adopting the budget, and would not discuss any amendments outside of parliament as the tax and spending plan was before lawmakers for their consideration.
"The union cabinet met today and adopted the budget as introduced in parliament," the spokesman said.

"The government looks forward to parliament adopting the budget which is already in possession of the house. Therefore, as the budget is the property of the house, any changes or amendments in the budget cannot be discussed outside the house."
Chidambaram introduced the budget, which would cut corporate and personal income taxes, on February 28 while in the government of ousted prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
The market-friendly budget, which set off a stock market rally, has been held hostage by political upheaval which led to Deve Gowda's downfall and the naming of Inder Kumar Gujral as his successor.
Parliament is scheduled to take up the budget during a session beginning on April 30.
Chidambaram has not been included in Gujral's cabinet as his party decided not to join the government.
But Chidambaram's regional Tamil Maanila Congress party was due to meet on April 27 to decide if it should reverse its decision to keep out of Gujral's government.
News that Chidambaram's party might join the government gave a lift to share prices on the Bombay exchange on Wednesday.
Gujral has kept the finance portfolio for himself, hoping that Chidambaram would return to the ruling United Front coalition.
